sources.projection: An attestation is useful only when verified; provenance links a concrete subject to where/how it was produced and does not itself prove the subject is secure.
rakl_mapping: a post-promotion receipt must bind a concrete repository subject/ref state
receipt existence is not equivalent to verification
sources.novelty_effect: subject-bound provenance and verification are established supply-chain practice

sources.projection: Artifact attestations bind claims to an explicit subject digest such as SHA-256.
rakl_mapping: promotion authority should be subject-identity specific rather than prose-specific

sources.projection: Verification checks that an attestation statement subject matches the digest of the artifact being evaluated.
rakl_mapping: claimed active revision must be checked against the actually observed active subject

sources.projection: For branch refs, a normal update is fast-forward only when the old destination is an ancestor of the new source; this preserves intervening history.
rakl_mapping: promotion replay should use a non-forced fast-forward and separately verify the resulting active ref

remaining_rakl_specific_question: How a recursively self-modifying research method prevents its own validation ledger from asserting a successful promotion when the active repository ref never actually moved.
